svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: macOS · Gallery · item view · a preview · the originals on a device nearby · 1310×800
svg.desc: Mirrors the Gallery's ITEM VIEW on the Mac with a PREVIEW in focus whose originals are on ANOTHER DEVICE OF THIS PICPLACE ACCOUNT, ON THE SAME NETWORK — the editor's preview page with the nearby offer (nearby originals, docs/nearby-originals-plan.md §7; Steven's brief of 2026-09-28: 'Preview only · The originals are only on iPhone for now · [Import originals from {Steve iPhone 18}]'; new 2026-09-28, drawn from the code; the iPhone's mirror of the same card is ../iOS/project-photo.viewer.preview.nearby.portrait.svg). Everything but the status card and tile 8's pill is gallery.item.preview.svg's. THE OFFER: `NearbyService.offer(for:shortfall:)` (App/Nearby/NearbyService.swift) — a device of this account that answered the holdings question with every original and is not busy; a Mac first, else the first to answer (N14) — reaches the page through `PicPlaceController.fetchOffer` (App/PicPlace/PicPlaceFetch.swift) as `.nearby(NearbyOffer, alsoOnPicPlace:)`, AHEAD OF PICPLACE (N12). It is shown only while that device answers — LetsLapse open on it, on the same network (N7, N15); LetsLapse closed there, or another network, and the card is the page's 'not uploaded yet' reading again: the same caption (PicPlace's presence record names the holder, not the network), the slashed camera, no button. The device's name is the other device's `DeviceName.current` (Shared/DeviceName.swift, N5) — a Mac's own computer name ('Steve's MacBook Pro'), a phone's or an iPad's model ('iPhone 18 Pro', 'iPad Air 13-inch (M3)') where iOS gives an app only the bare word. THE CARD, statusCard(style: .light) at y 237 — LL.cardBackground, radius 16, padding 12, VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10), no badge (the marquee badge is the dark card's): HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 10) { `StatusGlyphView(.asset(.originals, .nowhere), size 13, surface .adaptive)` (App/HoldingsPill.swift) — camera.fill with a slash knocked through and drawn over it (SF Symbols has no camera.slash), in the light palette's grey: not on this Mac, and not on PicPlace either (§16: slashed = nowhere reachable) — in its 18 pt column; VStack(spacing: 3) { the title `ProjectHoldings.Tier.label` 'Preview only' 13 pt semibold; the caption 11.5 pt #6D6D72 '\(subject) \(verb) only on \(nearby.deviceName) for now' → 'The originals are only on iPhone 18 Pro for now' }; Spacer(minLength: 8) } — no action in the row (the offer's action is full width), so the text column may take 228 pt (274 less the 18 pt glyph, two 10 pt gaps and the Spacer's 8) and the caption wraps there to two lines, 'for now' alone (CoreText: the first line 211.7; 'for' would need 230.2). Then `CardAction.importNearby`, the full-width button under the row: 'Import \(what) from \(nearby.deviceName)' → 'Import originals from iPhone 18 Pro' ('the originals' loses its article; a Photo capture's reads 'Import the full-size photo from …'), Text 14 pt semibold, lineLimit 2, centred, .frame(maxWidth: .infinity), 9 pt above and below, WHITE on LL.accent #C36A00 (the iPhone's dark card: black on amber) in a RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius 10) — 274 × 35 at y 306, its label one line (237.4 of 274). 298 × 116 at y 237: 12 + the row 47 (title 16 + 3 + the caption's two lines 28) + 10 + 35 + 12, each Text frame rounded up to the whole point. The press → `PicPlaceController.fetch` → `importNearby`: the same task slot, progress and Stop as a download (gallery.item.preview.importing.svg), landing on the Editor page. A click on the card's text does not ask here (the card asks only without an action, or with Download); the greyed controls do (gallery.item.preview.prompt.nearby.svg). WITH alsoOnPicPlace (PicPlace can supply them too; desc-only): the caption reads 'Editing needs the originals — on iPhone 18 Pro nearby, and on PicPlace · 214 files · 1,16 GB' — three lines in the 228 pt column, so the card is 130 pt — the camera grey (`.asset(.originals, .there)`, gallery.item.preview.svg's), the same button; the prompt then offers Download from PicPlace as well. A failed import's sentence (`NearbyService.importErrors`, the sending device's own words — 'iPhone 18 Pro stopped sending.') replaces the caption until the next press. SAMPLE: tile 8 of gallery.svg's grid — 'Stack 7. 9. at 21:40', 8 of 14, 214 JPEG originals (3024 × 4032 — INFO's Size), 1,16 GB recorded in assets.ndjson; the grade is a record, so the dots of Presets and Light still show — here in the state the nearby offer answers: a preview pulled from PicPlace whose originals were never uploaded; they are on the iPhone 18 Pro that shot them. So tile 8's pill is holdings-pill.nowhere.originals (holdingsPillState: the originals neither here nor on PicPlace → .nowhere; nothing heavy here and the originals not on PicPlace → no cloud — the pill does not look for devices nearby), drawn over the strip component as gallery.item.preview.downloading.svg draws its tile (the tile's art, the pill as a component reference at 0.8, 3 pt in, the ring). THE ITEM VIEW is gallery.item.svg's — the inspector column (GalleryPreviewPanel .inspector, 330 pt), the item header (▤ · ‹ Gallery · the name · 'n of N'), the editor column (the media beside the fixed 330 pt rail) and the filmstrip under everything, the floating tab bar — and GalleryItemEditor (App/GalleryItemView.swift) puts EditorPreviewPage in the editor's place when the focus request's asset is `.preview`: GalleryView.enterItem / move(to:) / step stage every project with `stageEditor(for:page:allowsPreview: true)`, so a preview opens, and the filmstrip and ← → walk straight through previews (they stalled on one until 2026-09-25). The page is its own view (EditorPreviewPageContent, plan T6), built from the editor's components with a `locked` state — never the editor mounted on a poster, so it has no write path (no persist net, no white migration, no as-shot reads). LAYOUT (App/EditorPreviewPage.swift railBody, the Mac's only dressing): the picture pane — black, the whole 648 × 568 column (no timeline strip, no full-screen button, no marquee badge: the badge is the dark card's) — with poster.jpg as it is (previewPictureURL; graded when it was made, never graded again), scaledToFit and centred: 426 × 568 at x 462; a Divider; the rail, a ScrollView padded 14 / 16 / 20 with 12 between — RailTabBar (App/RailTabBar.swift, locked: Text · Frames · Masks accent at 38 %, Editor selected), EditorGroupBar (.macCard, locked: every cell #6D6D72 at 42 %, none selected, the dots LL.accent at 55 %), then statusCard(style: .light) at y 237 — LL.cardBackground, radius 16, padding 12, no badge. Every greyed control stays clickable and ASKS (a click on a locked page → ask(.tab), a group → ask(.group), the card itself → ask(.line), subject 'Editing' — only while it offers Download or nothing, never beside this offer's button). macOS rounds each Text frame up to the whole point (measured: the stage-1 captures' cards are 57 and 85 pt, exactly the rounded sums), so the rest card is 85 pt where the unrounded arithmetic says 83.7. INSPECTOR as gallery.item.preview.svg's (metadata needs nothing local); its HERE row, past METADATA, reads 'Preview only — originals not on PicPlace yet'. HOOKS: the nearby bench (docs/nearby-originals-plan.md §12): a Mac scratch root (`-storage.libraryRootPath`) holding the preview — a pulled project, or `LL_DROP_SOURCES=<uuid>:originals` — and a Simulator holding the originals, both bound to one picplace.test account (`LL_PICPLACE_TOKENS` always, one token per install) and, before the server hands out the key, given the same `LL_NEARBY_KEY`; then `LL_TAB=gallery LL_ITEM=<uuid>` on the Mac with LetsLapse open on the Simulator — this reading needs a project whose originals PicPlace never received (with them on PicPlace too the card reads the alsoOnPicPlace caption); `LL_NEARBY_IMPORT=<uuid>` presses Import once a device offers it. The Mac copy needs Local Network permission (System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Local Network): refused, its browser and listener report NoAuth and the card never offers. Drawn from the code, not from a capture: a Mac importing is not benched yet (plan §15 — the Mac bench copy had no Local Network access). The words and glyphs are the code's; the card's seats are SwiftUI's own layout of statusCard's structure with these words, run offscreen on this Mac (the same structure gives the rest card 85 and the download 96, as gallery.item.preview.svg and gallery.item.preview.downloading.svg have them); the wraps are CoreText's at the column widths.

g.data-symbol: camera.fill + a slash knocked through (no SF camera.slash)

g.text: The originals are only on iPhone 18 Pro

mirrors EditorPreviewPage statusCard(.light) + CardAction.importNearby — NearbyService.offer → FetchOffer.nearby · LL_TAB=gallery LL_ITEM=<uuid> on the nearby bench
